To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the stringy partonic amplitudes are described by a finite number of universal functions and that these functions can be expressed in a compact way.

(i) The stringy amplitudes are expressed by the sum of two functions, one of them being the same for all processes, the other one being process-dependent and calculable for any model; (ii) the process-dependent part can be expressed in terms of a single function for all processes; (iii) the process-independent part is universal for all amplitudes involving gluon exchange, and is related in a simple way to the process-independent part of the four-gluon amplitude

the five-point amplitude is a sum of two functions, each of which is universal for the processes involving N gluons or N − 2gluons plus a quark–ant-quark pair, while the amplitudes with four fermions plus one gauge boson are model-dependent and depend on the geometry of the extra dimensions.
